card.title: My Support, My Say
card.instruction: Treat every past favor as a continuing investment in your right to influence present decisions.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I bought your bakery mixer. Save me a place at the menu tasting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was a birthday gift, not a share in the bakery.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I backed your cakes. I should taste what my support produces.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're switching to bread. Come Friday; the customers will choose.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll come Thursday. They should only choose between loaves I've approved.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 treats the gifted mixer as menu access, A3 defends continuing influence, and A5 demands preapproval even after the product changes.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's birthday-gift distinction produces A3's backing claim; B4's customer bread choice causes A5's earlier private screening.

relationship.evidence: B2 defines the gift's limits and B4 offers participation in an actual customer tasting.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's Friday customer vote to schedule Thursday control over the choices.

specificity.evidence: A1-B2 establish a bakery mixer given for a birthday; B4 states the switch to bread.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's Thursday answer earns its entitlement from B4's Friday invitation.
